links.note: The construction of buildings and roads placed in the secondary sector - this concept states it explicitly, alongside utilities and manufacturing. Already linked and correct.
Manufacturing in factories, processing raw material from the primary sector into another form - this concept's definition of the secondary sector. Already linked and correct.
Cotton used to make clothes - one of this concept's paired examples, each naming a primary activity on its left and a secondary activity on its right.
Doctors, nurses, teachers, lawyers and pilots providing their services - this concept's list of tertiary activities.
Warehouses glossed as large buildings used for storing products before they are sold, used or rented out to shops - this concept carries that gloss.
Milk spoiling or curdling very fast in hot weather, so the Anand farmers of the early 1940s had to sell it quickly - this concept's account of the problem that created the whole story.

The difference between primary and secondary - this concept draws it directly, milk derived from a natural source being primary and milk converted into powder, ghee and butter in factories being secondary. Already linked and correct.
Kautilya's line that the root of prosperity is economic activity - this concept opens the chapter on it.
The number of economic activities increasing tremendously over the decades, from agriculture and pottery to drones and software - this concept's contrast. Already linked and correct.
Cultivating grains on farms as the primary example, against manufacturing, banking and software - this concept's definition and list. Already linked and correct.
Collecting wood from the forests - one of this concept's primary activities, each taking something out of the natural world.
Extracting coal from mines - listed in this concept among the primary activities. Already linked and correct.
A cooperative glossed as a group of people who voluntarily come together to meet their economic and social needs, owning it themselves and deciding collectively - this concept carries that gloss.
AMUL set up in 1946 under Tribhuvandas Patel and Dr. Varghese Kurien - this concept names both. Already linked and correct.
The cooperative giving farmers control over the production and sale of milk, with tasks shared and income rising gradually - this concept's account of the benefit.
A factory glossed as a building or group of buildings where goods are manufactured or components put together to make a final product - this concept's gloss.
Export glossed as goods and services produced in one country and sold to buyers in another - this concept's gloss, placed just before the products leave Anand.
Farmers milking their cows to sell the milk called a primary sector activity because the product is derived directly from a natural source - this concept's classification. Already linked and correct.

The one visible pair defines a cooperative as a group for mutual economic and social benefit, which is this concept's gloss, and the other terms it glosses - middlemen and pasteurisation - are the ones such a matching set draws on. Most of the stem is missing from the item.
Monetary value glossed as the value of something that can be measured in terms of money - this concept carries that gloss while recalling the previous chapter.
The three main types of economic sector, primary, secondary and tertiary - this concept names them. Already linked and correct.
Primary activities defined as those in which people are directly dependent on nature to produce goods - this concept's definition, where the word directly carries the weight.
Construction of buildings and roads in the secondary sector - this concept's statement. Already linked and correct.
Manufacturing of products in factories and production units within the secondary sector - this concept's statement. Already linked and correct.
Wood from the forest converted into furniture and paper - one of this concept's paired examples of a secondary activity.
The tertiary sector also being called the service sector - this concept ends on that.
The driver of a truck transporting grains and vegetables from the farm to a factory or the market - this concept's first example of a tertiary activity.
